stem:
Chitra draws the square shown in the figure. She wants to count its lines of symmetry by testing folds.

How many lines of symmetry does the square have?

options.text: Infinitely many, because any line through the centre looks balanced at a glance.
Four folds are what create the square in the first place.
Four: two through midpoints of opposite sides and two through opposite corners, each passing the fold test.
The count needs group-theory language before any fold can be checked.

teacher.key_rationale: A square has four fold lines that give exact overlap: two midlines and two diagonals. Glancing balance without the fold test overcounts. Folds do not create the square. Group theory is outside the chapter.
teacher.figure_note: Unmarked square PQRS; learner counts fold lines.

mx_swap.reason: Mechanism-conflation CWO mixes rotational symmetry into a line-count hinge; kept condition_omission, relationship_reversal, scope_error on the fold-count idea.
